title: Act 3 — A Voyage to Arcturus research database

coverage.named_character_scope: C01–C38; aliases are merged. Maskull/Nightspore share identity I01. Deity aspects Faceny/Amfuse/Thire are additionally catalogued together in C44, related to C04.
coverage.excluded_name_scope: Named composers, staged Pharaoh, classical/religious comparison names and real place names are not additional plot characters. Arg is a creature common noun; Dolm is a color; Hator and Swaylone are people, not places.
coverage.art_note: Concept art is always game_proposal. visual_facts are primary-text features, not production art requirements.
coverage.named_character_records_note: 38 named character/appearance rows C01–C38 include Maskull and Nightspore linked as identity I01; Krag/Surtur and Crystalman/Shaping/Faceny/Gangnet are merged. C44 adds named Threal aspects Amfuse/Thire without asserting separate ultimate gods.

entities.title: Maskull
entities.name: Maskull
entities.description: The Earth traveller follows successive people and philosophies across Tormance. His apparent independence repeatedly fails; he kills several people under altered moral perceptions. At the end Krag identifies him with Nightspore, and Maskull dies as Nightspore reappears.
entities.visual_facts: Very large and broad; heavy carved-looking features, full beard, short bristling black hair, small black eyes. His Tormance organs change by region.
entities.game_adaptation: Reference silhouette and moral journey; the campaign’s established playable character is retained.
entities.notes: Maskull and Nightspore have separate narrative appearances but share identity group I01; do not count them as two unrelated souls.

entities.title: Nightspore
entities.name: Nightspore
entities.description: Maskull’s reserved companion on Earth and the awakened traveller of the final chapter. He climbs the Muspel tower and learns the false world’s mechanism before choosing to return to the struggle with Krag.
entities.visual_facts: Middle height, tough body, hairless face, wild distant eyes and an expression of spiritual hunger. Tweeds in the Earth frame.
entities.game_adaptation: Witness or revelation figure; not a rival boss.
entities.notes: Ch20 makes Maskull/Nightspore’s identity relation explicit; retain two appearance records for drawing references with one identity group.

entities.title: Krag / Surtur
entities.name: Krag / Surtur
entities.description: Krag interrupts the séance and takes the travellers to Tormance. His harsh and painful interventions oppose Crystalman. The ending confirms that Krag is Surtur and that his name on Earth is pain.
entities.visual_facts: Shortish thick man with immense muscular development and an oversized head; beardless yellow face combining brutality, humour and sagacity. Piercing disagreeable voice. Surtur’s early apparent forms are visionary and inconsistent.
entities.game_adaptation: Severe guide, drumming/revelation motif; never label him the final evil to defeat.
entities.notes: Early speakers identify Surtur with Shaping in error. Ch8’s splendid vision calling itself Surtur is not a reliable portrait of the final truth.

entities.title: Crystalman / Shaping
entities.name: Crystalman / Shaping
entities.description: The maker worshipped under benevolent names is exposed as the being that captures and degrades the Muspel stream into pleasure-seeking individual wills. Gangnet is a late tempting appearance. Faceny and the other Threal divine figures belong to the false-world revelation.
entities.visual_facts: A recurring horrible grin on dead faces. Gangnet appears handsome and soothing; the final presence is a vast bright, nebulous shadow with no definite shape or color.
entities.game_adaptation: Final local manifestation may become a readable combat boss; breaking it opens a route rather than annihilating the universe.
entities.notes: Keep belief, vision and final revelation distinct. A literal crystal-armored humanoid is an art invention, not the novel’s body description. Amfuse/Thire are named Threal aspects grouped in C44.

entities.title: Backhouse
entities.name: Backhouse
entities.description: Professional medium hired for Faull’s séance. His materialisation is interrupted by Krag; his professional confidence contrasts with the guests’ theatrical expectations.
entities.visual_facts: Small, thickset, pointed beard; fresh and sane appearance, controlled manner.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional Earth-frame journal/intro portrait; not hostile.

entities.title: Montague Faull
entities.name: Montague Faull
entities.description: Wealthy South American merchant and host of the séance at his Hampstead house Prolands. His staged entertainment and bored manner frame the uncanny intrusion.
entities.visual_facts: Prominent clear-cut features, metallic-looking skin, bored impassiveness; lounging posture and expensive domestic surroundings.
entities.game_adaptation: Earth-frame reference vignette.

entities.title: Mrs. Jameson
entities.name: Mrs. Jameson
entities.description: Faull’s sister, serving as his hostess. Her cultivated emotional response to music and the séance contrasts with Faull’s detachment.
entities.visual_facts: Small patrician features, porcelain-like hands; seated near a pianoforte.
entities.game_adaptation: Earth-frame portrait; no invented given name.

entities.title: Kent-Smith
entities.name: Kent-Smith
entities.description: Retired magistrate among the séance guests, known for judicial humour. He discusses his autobiography and the safeguards against deception.
entities.visual_facts: Well past seventy; disconcertingly bright eyes and preference for a comfortable chair.
entities.game_adaptation: Earth-frame journal portrait.

entities.title: Prior
entities.name: Prior
entities.description: Prosperous City coffee importer attending the séance. He tries to make the company jovial and later inspects the stage scenery.
entities.visual_facts: Atmosphere of wine and tobacco; otherwise little fixed bodily description.
entities.game_adaptation: Earth-frame minor cast; do not invent a canonical costume beyond the social setting.

entities.title: Lang
entities.name: Lang
entities.description: Stockjobber and amateur conjurer, asked to search the séance setting and the medium for hidden apparatus.
entities.visual_facts: Tall, thin, becoming bald; quiet scrutiny.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional detail on scepticism and the séance’s physical arrangements.

entities.title: Professor Halbart
entities.name: Professor Halbart
entities.description: Psychologist, author and lecturer on mental aspects of crime, insanity and genius, attending the séance.
entities.visual_facts: Small, meagre-looking and mild-mannered; stubborn intellectual disposition.
entities.game_adaptation: Earth-frame minor portrait.

entities.title: Mrs. Trent
entities.name: Mrs. Trent
entities.description: Guest who decorates the séance room and invites Maskull and Nightspore. Her relationship with Faull is suggested through glances and intimacy rather than fully explained.
entities.visual_facts: About twenty-eight; white face, smooth black hair, full crimson lips, tall graceful body, costly clothes.
entities.game_adaptation: Earth-frame scene reference; no invented given name.

entities.title: Mr. Trent
entities.name: Mr. Trent
entities.description: Trent is mentioned as not attending the séance; he does not appear in the action.
entities.visual_facts: No appearance is provided.
entities.game_adaptation: Text-only reference, or clearly marked invented portrait.
entities.notes: Usually read as Mrs. Trent’s husband, but the short mention does not supply a portrait or first name; relationship is an inference from naming/context.

entities.title: Joiwind
entities.name: Joiwind
entities.description: Poolingdred resident who finds Maskull helpless, exchanges blood with him, offers food-free hospitality and prays for purity. She and Panawe avoid consuming or injuring living things.
entities.visual_facts: Tall, slight, graceful; long loosely plaited flaxen hair; delicately changing opalescent skin, forehead breve, paired poigns and magn tentacle. Milky opalescent blood.
entities.game_adaptation: Compassionate witness or rest-space host, not enemy; character art may adapt modest clothing while retaining sensory organs.

entities.title: Panawe
entities.name: Panawe
entities.description: Joiwind’s husband recounts his childhood, his sister’s sacrifice within their shared body and his encounters with Broodviol, Slofork and Muremaker. His reverence for life explains his abstention from killing.
entities.visual_facts: Young, white hair and snowy skin, black quiet eyes; beardless, white clothing, breve/poigns/magn. Stern features soften toward Joiwind.
entities.game_adaptation: Contemplative witness and route counsel; do not turn his nonviolence into a mandatory combat tutorial.

entities.title: Broodviol
entities.name: Broodviol
entities.description: Old sage of Wombflash, encountered in Panawe’s childhood story and later recalled by Polecrab. He gives a mistaken account of the struggle between the sexes in Panawe and dies after Alppain begins reaching his region.
entities.visual_facts: Gnarled sturdy elder; trilateral body with three legs, three arms and six evenly distributed eyes. About 120 Tormance years in Panawe’s recollection.
entities.game_adaptation: Rare character sheet or remembered silhouette; the novel presents him retrospectively, not as a living Act 3 combatant.

entities.title: Slofork
entities.name: Slofork
entities.description: Sorcerer met in Panawe’s story, skilled in budding and removing bodily organs. He challenges Panawe’s understanding of pleasure, pain, love and the world beyond Shaping.
entities.visual_facts: Bright gamboge skin and extremely long proboscis-like nose.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional lore witness. His self-amputation anecdote is reported, not shown as a player action.

entities.title: Oceaxe
entities.name: Oceaxe
entities.description: Ifdawn woman who leads Maskull through its unstable mountains, draws him into desire and encourages the removal of her lover/husband Crimtyphon. Tydomin subsequently compels her fatal leap.
entities.visual_facts: Powerful handsome face, muscular graceful limbs, sorb forehead eye, third arm from the chest, large animal-skin garment.
entities.game_adaptation: Ambiguous guide portrait; not automatically a boss.

entities.title: Crimtyphon
entities.name: Crimtyphon
entities.description: Oceaxe’s boylike lover/husband uses his will to force Sature into becoming a fruit tree. Maskull kills him. Tydomin also claims him as her husband and carries his corpse.
entities.visual_facts: Small boylike form, smooth soft childish features, yellow-ivory skin; violet curling hair and violet sinister adult sorb. Rough skin garment, moss couch, plums and ironic serenity.
entities.game_adaptation: Candidate transmutation boss based on his domination, not a new species.

entities.title: Tydomin
entities.name: Tydomin
entities.description: Crimtyphon’s other wife drives Oceaxe to death, manipulates Maskull’s will, prompts his absorption of Digrung and tries to use his body. After meeting Spadevil she renounces her former cruelty and accepts sacrifice.
entities.visual_facts: Slight middle-height figure; pale face, clustered neck-length indigo hair, dark sad sorb; tunic/breeches made of blue-green reptile plates.
entities.game_adaptation: Candidate coercion/echo boss for an alternate campaign; later change of heart remains visible.
entities.notes: Not merely a seductive villain. Her transformation and death belong to the novel’s moral instability.

entities.title: Digrung
entities.name: Digrung
entities.description: Traveller from Matterplay and Joiwind’s brother. He threatens to report Maskull’s conduct to his sister; under Tydomin’s influence Maskull absorbs him. His residual presence later troubles Maskull in Matterplay.
entities.visual_facts: Changing skin color, recognisable resemblance to Joiwind, dry nervous voice.
entities.game_adaptation: Journal victim/identity echo; no hostile regular-enemy conversion.

entities.title: Spadevil
entities.name: Spadevil
entities.description: Reformer taking a new law into Sant, grants Maskull and Tydomin double forehead probes and teaches existence for things rather than possession of things. Catice rejects his doctrine and Maskull kills him.
entities.visual_facts: Middle-aged, dark solid body, stern heavy brow, black beard, projecting chin, twin flat forehead membranes.
entities.game_adaptation: Witness of altered judgment or optional ideological scene; doctrine is a claim, not a universally verified metaphysics.

entities.title: Hator
entities.name: Hator
entities.description: Ancient teacher whose followers in Sant use pain to shield the soul from pleasure. Spadevil argues that later followers have turned this into vanity and pride.
entities.visual_facts: Historical figure; no direct portrait is supplied.
entities.game_adaptation: Lore reference, not a present-day boss.
entities.notes: Separate Hator’s philosophy from his followers’ practice and Spadevil’s critique.

entities.title: Maulger
entities.name: Maulger
entities.description: Sant authority whom Spadevil sets out to find; Catice announces that Maulger is dead.
entities.visual_facts: No direct appearance provided.
entities.game_adaptation: Text-only historical reference; do not fabricate a canon fight.

entities.title: Catice
entities.name: Catice
entities.description: Maulger’s successor confronts Spadevil at Sant’s pool. His doctrine of rejection drives Maskull toward the killings of Spadevil and Tydomin; he also gives Maskull the name Muspel.
entities.visual_facts: Powerful bowed elder, long heavy trunk, short legs, lemon-colored deeply rutted beardless face, sparse black hair, one forehead membrane, scant loincloth and trifork.
entities.game_adaptation: Candidate ascetic arena boss if needed; selected campaign leaves him a reference.

entities.title: Dreamsinter
entities.name: Dreamsinter
entities.description: Strange forest seer encountered in Wombflash. He leads Maskull after Surtur’s drumming and shows a vision linking Maskull, Krag and Nightspore.
entities.visual_facts: Gigantic nearly naked build, taller than Maskull by a head; faintly phosphorescent body, three luminous pale-green eyes, hairless skin, thick black hair coiled and fastened, staff.
entities.game_adaptation: Unsettling guide or brief projection; vision text must remain a vision.

entities.title: Polecrab
entities.name: Polecrab
entities.description: Fisherman on the Sinking Sea who trains arg animals, receives Maskull, recalls Broodviol and tries to prevent Gleameil’s dangerous musical journey.
entities.visual_facts: Oldish, short thick sturdy body, short legs, long powerful arms and huge hands; bald head/face, slablike wrinkled walnut-colored leathery face, three eyes jade-green/blue/ulfire, rough hide garment.
entities.game_adaptation: Shore witness and rest tableau; not a combat boss.

entities.title: Gleameil
entities.name: Gleameil
entities.description: Polecrab’s wife and mother of three boys follows her inner hunger for Earthrid’s music. She accompanies Maskull to Swaylone’s Island and dies during the music.
entities.visual_facts: Young, tall, slender and erect, lightly tanned and strong; three great glowing eyes, masses of yellow hair coiled carelessly with loose strands; refined energetic face and hide garment.
entities.game_adaptation: Musical tragedy and self-directed desire; retain her agency rather than using her as a repeated escort objective.

entities.title: Earthrid
entities.name: Earthrid
entities.description: Musician on Swaylone’s Island who plays the lake Irontick by disturbing its surface. The music proves fatal to Gleameil. Maskull takes over and destroys the instrument; he later finds Earthrid’s mutilated corpse on the shore.
entities.visual_facts: Young middle age, pale weak vacant face with disagreeable expression, sparse black hair on head/chin, circular convoluted ear-like forehead organ. In moonlight the face acquires crafty grandeur.
entities.game_adaptation: Strong candidate music-arena boss; lake as instrument is canonical, combat pulse warnings are invented.

entities.title: Swaylone
entities.name: Swaylone
entities.description: Legendary first musician of Tormance, said by Gleameil to have settled the island in a remote age. The legend links music, Shaping and Krag.
entities.visual_facts: No direct contemporary appearance; images of him would interpret a narrated legend.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional lore portrait or relief; not an additional present boss.
entities.notes: Record as legend, not a verified scene witnessed by Maskull.

entities.title: Leehallfae
entities.name: Leehallfae
entities.description: Ancient surviving phaen searching for Faceny in the life streams of Matterplay. Ae joins Maskull in finding Threal, but dies and dissolves on entering that region.
entities.visual_facts: Strangely luminous copper-colored skin; angular/faceted limbs and irregular beardless face, two eyes, ankle-length single braid, dark frocklike knee-length garment and turban hiding a forehead organ. Vigorous youthfulness with immeasurable ancientness.
entities.game_adaptation: Guide/witness preserving the distinct third positive sex. Use ae/aer/aerself; no gender-changing reward system.
entities.notes: Narrator initially uses a feminine impression, then explicitly coins ae. Leehallfae is neither male nor female and is not described as sexless.

entities.title: Corpang
entities.name: Corpang
entities.description: Threal ascetic worshipping Faceny, Amfuse and Thire. After their divine appearances prove false, he follows Maskull toward Muspel-light and accompanies him through Lichstorm until their ways part.
entities.visual_facts: Short thickset but emaciated; hairless coarse energetic face, wide brow, short hair, sanguine eyes; black sleeveless robe and long staff.
entities.game_adaptation: Doubting companion; not a boss merely because his doctrine is severe.

entities.title: Haunte
entities.name: Haunte
entities.description: Lichstorm man who travels in a skin boat sustained by male stones, shelters the travellers at Sarclash and takes them to Sullenbode. Maskull steals his protecting light; Haunte then dies on kissing her.
entities.visual_facts: Young middle-height man with a disproportionately long trunk and immense deep chest; sharp pointed ugly hairless face, protruding teeth, upward-slanting eyes/brows, stump-like forehead organ, short thin hair, dolm skin, close-fitting fur garment.
entities.game_adaptation: Dangerous companion reference; a proposed wind-boat fight conflicts with the ground-only game and is not selected.
entities.notes: The protecting light comes from the male stones; a forehead lamp is not a verified canonical accessory.

entities.title: Sullenbode
entities.name: Sullenbode
entities.description: Lichstorm woman awakened fully by Maskull’s kiss. She guides him toward Adage and accepts the risk of accompanying his search. Her life depends on his continuing love; when it fails she dies and he buries her.
entities.visual_facts: Tall slight and slow-moving; softly glowing exposed skin, long pale face, heavy brows, fiery gashlike mouth; black eyes and dark maroon hair.
entities.game_adaptation: Her projected likeness may appear in an invented garden manifestation; it is not damageable, and the human figure is not the boss target.
entities.notes: No canonical garden or root boss exists. Sullenbode is a guide and sacrificing lover, not an ordinary hostile monster.

entities.title: Lodd
entities.name: Lodd
entities.description: Earlier traveller seeking Muspel-light, recalled by Haunte as having passed toward Adage five years previously.
entities.visual_facts: Proud, noble and exceptionally different in Haunte’s memory; no secure detailed anatomy.
entities.game_adaptation: Text or remembered silhouette, not a mandatory rescue objective.

entities.title: Muremaker
entities.name: Muremaker
entities.description: Cruel sorb-user met in Panawe’s story, suspended over a thousand-foot gulf by Nuclamp after a dispute over a woman. Panawe refuses to save the habitual tormentor.
entities.visual_facts: Ogrelike suspended upright figure, wry grimace and scraping voice.
entities.game_adaptation: Candidate remembered coercion encounter; no direct present-day appearance.

entities.title: Nuclamp
entities.name: Nuclamp
entities.description: Offstage rival who holds Muremaker suspended by force of will, according to Muremaker’s account in Panawe’s story.
entities.visual_facts: No direct appearance supplied.
entities.game_adaptation: Lore-only reference or clearly invented silhouette.

entities.title: Sature
entities.name: Sature
entities.description: Crimtyphon’s living victim, compelled toward rooting and becoming a fruit tree while his responses are dictated by his captor.
entities.visual_facts: Short muscular man with broad bearded commonplace face distorted by pain, despair and horror; buds beginning at his feet.
entities.game_adaptation: Victim/reference image for domination, not a plant-enemy species.

entities.title: Arg animals
entities.name: Arg animals
entities.description: Seal-like six-legged fishing animals bred and trained by Polecrab. The word arg is used as a species/common noun; his command to one is not evidence of a unique proper name.
entities.visual_facts: About two feet long, six clawed legs; broad-headed animals learn better but swim more slowly.
entities.game_adaptation: Peaceful shore ecology; not all alien creatures should attack.
entities.notes: Includes Polecrab’s trained individual. Catalogue does not mistake capitalisation in a command for a new named person.

entities.title: Phaens
entities.name: Phaens
entities.description: A former people represented by Leehallfae, with a positive third sex distinct from male and female. Leehallfae considers aer self the surviving member of the former world.
entities.visual_facts: Neither male nor female; Leehallfae is the visual primary reference.
entities.game_adaptation: Respect source pronouns and singular survivor; crowds of present phaens would be invention.

entities.title: Panawe’s family and twin sister
entities.name: Panawe’s family and twin sister
entities.description: Panawe recounts travel with his contemplative father and active Poolingdred mother. He describes a female twin sharing his childhood body and sacrificing herself rather than fighting him for existence.
entities.visual_facts: Parents have contrasting temperaments; the sister has no independent external body portrait.
entities.game_adaptation: Text-only family reference or explicitly interpretive dual silhouette.
entities.notes: Broodviol’s account of violent sex competition is contradicted by Panawe’s own understanding.

entities.title: Séance materialisation
entities.name: Séance materialisation
entities.description: Backhouse produces a human-shaped materialisation at the séance. Krag breaks its neck; the dead appearance takes on a dreadful grin associated with Crystalman.
entities.visual_facts: Young and beautiful human semblance; changing ominous expression after death.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional uncanny prologue reference.
entities.notes: Not Backhouse himself, and not an authenticated separate named god.

entities.title: Polecrab and Gleameil’s three sons
entities.name: Polecrab and Gleameil’s three sons
entities.description: Three boys say farewell before Gleameil’s crossing. The oldest carries the youngest, and Polecrab discusses their differing temperaments.
entities.visual_facts: Different ages; youngest pale/slight with tawny gold eyes and intermittently perplexed expression.
entities.game_adaptation: Shore family vignette; no escort combat.

entities.title: Faceny, Amfuse and Thire — the Three Figures
entities.name: Faceny, Amfuse and Thire — the Three Figures
entities.description: Corpang describes three interpenetrating worlds: existence/Faceny, relation or love/Amfuse, and feeling or worship/Thire. Three statues become divine visions; after Maskull’s light fades their faces expose the deceptive grin.
entities.visual_facts: Three immense rock figures and translucent visionary persons with their own visual manifestations.
entities.game_adaptation: False-authority tableau, not three additional required bosses.
entities.notes: The three names are catalogued together as aspects of the false world; Faceny is also named as Shaping/Crystalman by Leehallfae. They are not three independent rescuing gods.

entities.title: Unnamed Earth attendants and anecdotal roles
entities.name: Unnamed Earth attendants and anecdotal roles
entities.description: The novel contains unnamed parents, servants, orchestra members and people cited within conversations. These supporting roles have no separate names or character arcs in the primary cast.
entities.visual_facts: Specific designs are mostly unspecified.
entities.game_adaptation: Background only.
entities.notes: Coverage record for roles; this is not an invented additional named cast.

entities.title: Sunbound Stalker
entities.name: Sunbound Stalker
entities.description: Invented regular enemy that braces toward one short lunge lane, locks it, then lunges once; its low flank remains slashable during recovery in both sun states.
entities.visual_facts: Art proposal: compact legible silhouette using the twin-sun contrast.
entities.game_adaptation: Read the short lane, choose a ground dash landing beside the commitment, then slash its low flank. Sun state changes scenery, not the recovery hitbox.
entities.notes: No creature with this name exists in the novel.

entities.title: Root Latcher
entities.name: Root Latcher
entities.description: Invented rooted bulb that previews one bounded crescent or short strip, sends its visible attack along that footprint, then exposes a low knot during recovery.
entities.visual_facts: Art proposal: low rootlike body; vulnerable knot above the floor.
entities.game_adaptation: Avoid the committed crescent/strip by a ground dash and slash the low knot. It never unpredictably immobilises or binds the player.
entities.notes: Inspired by prolific Matterplay ecology; hostile roots are not canonical.

entities.title: Mirror Echo
entities.name: Mirror Echo
entities.description: Invented echo that previews and replays its own authored dash and slash once, leaves a harmless hollow reflection, then exposes a rooted endpoint knot.
entities.visual_facts: Art proposal: one distinct translucent echo silhouette with floor-safe tell.
entities.game_adaptation: Read its own preview and punish the endpoint knot; this regular enemy does not capture the player’s prior action.
entities.notes: No named mirror-echo enemy exists in the novel.

entities.title: Prolands and the séance room
entities.name: Prolands and the séance room
entities.description: Faull’s Hampstead house contains a forty-by-twenty-foot lounge arranged as an auditorium before a stage replica of the Magic Flute temple scene.
entities.visual_facts: Brocade curtain, armchairs, electric brackets, carpet, seated pharaoh scenery, carved couch and hidden orchestra.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional journal/prologue rather than spending a full main level on Earth.

entities.title: Hampstead street
entities.name: Hampstead street
entities.description: After the séance the travellers talk under a star-filled March night sky before arranging departure to Starkness.
entities.visual_facts: Dark urban street and cold starfield.
entities.game_adaptation: Brief transition frame.

entities.title: Starkness observatory
entities.name: Starkness observatory
entities.description: Abandoned northern Scottish observatory near the North Sea and Haillar Station, used as the departure site.
entities.visual_facts: Neglected house, isolated coast, observatory tower and bare scientific rooms.
entities.game_adaptation: Arrival/departure reference, optional level kit reuse.

entities.title: Starkness tower
entities.name: Starkness tower
entities.description: An increasingly heavy climb and extraordinary optical experiences foreshadow the final tower. The travellers prepare their crystal torpedo there.
entities.visual_facts: Stone spiral stair, windows, changing burden and back-ray apparatus.
entities.game_adaptation: Structural foreshadowing; actual jumping/climbing need not be introduced.

entities.title: Tormance
entities.name: Tormance
entities.description: The inhabited world reached near Arcturus contains two suns, region-dependent ecology and bodily faculties. Maskull’s journey takes four Tormance days before the final awakening.
entities.visual_facts: Alien landforms, impossible extra colors and changing bodily perceptions.
entities.game_adaptation: Compress the journey into the act’s five levels; preserve ground navigation.

entities.title: Branchspell and Alppain — twin suns
entities.name: Branchspell and Alppain — twin suns
entities.description: Branchspell is the white sun; Alppain is blue. Their light produces two sets of primary colors sharing blue, and Alppain has a distinct effect on will and emotional perception.
entities.visual_facts: White/blue disk contrast; extraordinary skylight and white daylight shadows under Alppain.
entities.game_adaptation: Representational palettes and clearly signalled scenery transitions. Never hide attack warnings under lighting.

entities.title: Poolingdred
entities.name: Poolingdred
entities.description: Poolingdred itself is the cup-shaped mountain and shelter of Joiwind and Panawe. The journey to it begins on the scarlet desert sands where Maskull wakes, passing low wooded hills and strange flora.
entities.visual_facts: Poolingdred cup/crater mountain and cave shelter; on its approach, scarlet sand, black-stemmed purple shrubs, dark-mould hills, purple trees and blue egglike fruit.
entities.game_adaptation: Open first-level ground pockets; no repeat input tutorial.

entities.title: Shaping’s Well
entities.name: Shaping’s Well
entities.description: A natural amphitheatre encloses a black-trunked tree with transparent crystal leaves and a well of gnawl water where Joiwind prays to Shaping.
entities.visual_facts: Red-sand centre, enclosing small wooded hills, black-trunked tree and transparent crystal leaves. Shrine well water is dark green; gnawl water in Poolingdred is crystal clear.
entities.game_adaptation: Sanctuary imagery whose reassuring interpretation may later change.
entities.notes: Distinguish the desert shrine/approach from Poolingdred itself; blood-red water is not canonical.

entities.title: Lusion Plain
entities.name: Lusion Plain
entities.description: Maskull crosses the broad plain between Poolingdred and Ifdawn, encountering a vision calling itself Surtur and the sleeping Oceaxe.
entities.visual_facts: Open plain, looming distant mountains, isolated crimson jewel-like light and immense visionary cloud form.
entities.game_adaptation: Short broad transition within the first main level.

entities.title: Ifdawn Marest
entities.name: Ifdawn Marest
entities.description: Mountains undergo rapid upheavals, collapsing, rising and changing the paths between settlements. Oceaxe leads Maskull through this dangerous country.
entities.visual_facts: Castellated cliffs in vermilion, emerald, yellow, ulfire and black; deep chasms and moving mountain masses.
entities.game_adaptation: Spectacular movement outside active floor; telegraphed preset transformations between completed encounters.

entities.title: Disscourn
entities.name: Disscourn
entities.description: Great pyramidlike mountain overlooking the wider land; Tydomin’s cave and the route to Sant are on or beside it.
entities.visual_facts: Stupendous bright crags, cloud-sea views and rough boulder/gully paths.
entities.game_adaptation: Ground terraces with generous landing pockets; no required mountain-climbing subsystem.

entities.title: Tydomin’s cavern
entities.name: Tydomin’s cavern
entities.description: Tydomin leads Maskull to her dwelling with Crimtyphon’s corpse and uses him in her attempted exchange of bodies.
entities.visual_facts: Enclosed rocky cavern above a sea of clouds.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional coercion vignette or reference kit; do not repeat the literal body theft as mandatory new input.

entities.title: Sant
entities.name: Sant
entities.description: Cold bare upland associated with Hator’s ascetic doctrine; women are excluded. Spadevil seeks to change its law.
entities.visual_facts: Green snow, gusts, fog, bare severe plateau and little shelter.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional austerity palette and short doctrinal tableau.

entities.title: Sant pool and precipice
entities.name: Sant pool and precipice
entities.description: Catice stands in a pool in austere practice before his confrontation with Spadevil; the plateau overlooks Wombflash.
entities.visual_facts: Lonely water, trifork, bare ground and forest far below.
entities.game_adaptation: Boss candidate arena if Catice is used in an alternate pacing plan.

entities.title: Wombflash Forest
entities.name: Wombflash Forest
entities.description: Immense widely separated trees form a silent, damp, almost afterlife-like hall. Maskull recognises his crimes and encounters Dreamsinter with distant drumming.
entities.visual_facts: House-wide boles, branches far above the floor, wet leaves and mist, no dense underbrush. Panawe recalls dark red trunks and pale ulfire leaves.
entities.game_adaptation: Wide floor combat pockets amid gigantic trunks; keep dead-leaf ground continuous.
entities.notes: Ch13 verifies huge widely separated trunks, no underbrush, dead wet leaves, mist and distant sunlit tops. Dark red trunks/pale ulfire leaves are verified in Panawe’s ch7 recollection. Flesh-bark, embedded eyes, violet/pink canopy, thorn-root hostility and glowing attack marks are game-art additions.

entities.title: Sinking Sea
entities.name: Sinking Sea
entities.description: Sea adjoining Wombflash with perilously variable density. In some places Maskull can swim, in others can barely stay above water, and in others cannot force himself under. There is no visible sign of which water is ahead.
entities.visual_facts: Colored water, currents, pinnacles and island horizon.
entities.game_adaptation: Scenic boundary; no swimming or fatal arbitrary water-edge collision required.

entities.title: Polecrab’s inlet and shore
entities.name: Polecrab’s inlet and shore
entities.description: Fisherman’s creek beside the forest shelters his family, cooking sands, raft and trained arg.
entities.visual_facts: Shore bank, sheltered creek, cooking sand, pole raft and fishing animal.
entities.game_adaptation: Brief safe witness/rest vignette.

entities.title: Swaylone’s Island
entities.name: Swaylone’s Island
entities.description: Island reached by Maskull and Gleameil, named for legendary first music and inhabited by Earthrid.
entities.visual_facts: Strange coast, hills enclosing a small circular lake; moonlight after music.
entities.game_adaptation: Island shore arena can be ground-based; crossing represented as transition.

entities.title: Irontick
entities.name: Irontick
entities.description: Circular lake roughly half a mile across is Earthrid’s musical instrument, played through waves and disturbances on its surface. Maskull’s performance destroys it.
entities.visual_facts: Smooth circular water, concentric/interfering ripples, enclosing hills; water can act as a playing surface in the novel.
entities.game_adaptation: Static walkable shoreline/arena and visible pulse footprints are game inventions.

entities.title: Matterplay
entities.name: Matterplay
entities.description: Bare hills contain extremely fertile valleys whose life streams coin rapidly changing organisms. Maskull observes spectacular bodily transformations and meets Leehallfae.
entities.visual_facts: Dense unique flowers/plants, shallow broad streams, winged reptiles, huge insect forms and rock-framed jeweled valleys.
entities.game_adaptation: Ecological transformation outside bounded floor; small invented root threats use known controls.

entities.title: Threal
entities.name: Threal
entities.description: Subterranean country reached through a revealed cavity. It is airlit without a sky, and Leehallfae cannot survive its atmosphere.
entities.visual_facts: Jetlike ground, shadowless subdued light, grey-white huge shafts and strange trees.
entities.game_adaptation: False-sanctuary vignette; atmosphere as mood instead of oxygen-resource management.

entities.title: The Three Figures of Threal
entities.name: The Three Figures of Threal
entities.description: Earlier people erected three immense carved figures; Corpang’s prayers invoke their apparent living divine forms.
entities.visual_facts: Rock colossi, valley and translucent luminous apparitions.
entities.game_adaptation: Reference for false authority and final visual language; not compulsory triple boss.

entities.title: Lichstorm Range
entities.name: Lichstorm Range
entities.description: Mountains have fantastically overhanging caps, green snow and a lich wind that excites painful sexual passion.
entities.visual_facts: Hanging summit caps, mist, green snow and electric atmosphere.
entities.game_adaptation: Late-act atmosphere; use stable readable floor despite floating rock scenery.

entities.title: Sarclash
entities.name: Sarclash
entities.description: Haunte’s home mountain forms a horseshoe with westward ends and a mile or more between them. Its northern end joins the ridge toward Adage.
entities.visual_facts: Horseshoe mass, cliffs, capped peaks and large central valley.
entities.game_adaptation: Mountain framing for the fourth-level route.

entities.title: Haunte’s cave
entities.name: Haunte’s cave
entities.description: Cave in Sarclash where Haunte receives the travellers and recounts Lodd’s earlier search for Muspel-light.
entities.visual_facts: Cliff cave, shelter, male stones/light and the wind boat nearby.
entities.game_adaptation: Short witness room; no boat-combat production requirement.

entities.title: Sullenbode’s tree and glade
entities.name: Sullenbode’s tree and glade
entities.description: The travellers meet Sullenbode seated under a glowing fruit tree beneath Sarclash’s hanging cap. Her garment runs from one-shoulder cloak to loose knee-short breeches. After the kisses and awakening she guides them toward Adage.
entities.visual_facts: Huge tree with glowing branches, no leaves and red fruits hanging like lanterns; dimly shining grass under Sarclash’s cap. Sullenbode sits asleep cross-legged, holding partly eaten fruit.
entities.game_adaptation: The Garden boss is a separate fabricated enclosure inspired by attachment; a botanical death garden is not in the novel.

entities.title: Mornstab Pass
entities.name: Mornstab Pass
entities.description: Broad landslip descends from the ridge between Sarclash and Adage toward Barey. Maskull buries Sullenbode near it after their separation in spirit.
entities.visual_facts: Great sloping pass between dark precipices, hot spring, damp rocky/boggy ground and a small grave.
entities.game_adaptation: Late quiet transition; no precise cliff-edge platforming.

entities.title: Adage
entities.name: Adage
entities.description: Mountain associated with occasional Muspel-light, sought by Lodd and Corpang and approached with Sullenbode.
entities.visual_facts: Remote exceptionally high mass beyond the descending ridge.
entities.game_adaptation: Destination image; no claim that the game literally reaches the canonical summit.

entities.title: Barey
entities.name: Barey
entities.description: Low country beyond the mountains leads to the Ocean; Krag and the soothing Gangnet accompany Maskull across it.
entities.visual_facts: Intermixed water and land, blue-tinted morning haze and a riverside boat house.
entities.game_adaptation: False tranquility before final confrontation.

entities.title: Surtur’s Ocean and floating island
entities.name: Surtur’s Ocean and floating island
entities.description: Krag names the Ocean only as Maskull nears death. A small island raft carries the party through thickening fog toward Muspel.
entities.visual_facts: Transparent glasslike sea, fog, tiny drifting land raft and hidden horizon.
entities.game_adaptation: Narrative crossing after a ground arena; no new steering gesture.

entities.title: Muspel
entities.name: Muspel
entities.description: Source of fiery spirit beyond Crystalman’s false world; its light is experienced as emotion or passion. The final revelation frames an ongoing perilous struggle rather than an easy victory.
entities.visual_facts: Fierce doorlike light in a limitless black wall; inside, darkness and burning passion.
entities.game_adaptation: Final local breach and revelation, not conventional jewel-covered heaven.

entities.title: Muspel tower and six windows
entities.name: Muspel tower and six windows
entities.description: Nightspore climbs exhausting circular stone steps through six windows that progressively reveal the imprisoned life, Crystalman’s mechanism and the struggle. The roof is small and surrounded by darkness.
entities.visual_facts: Cold stone spiral staircase, high embrasures, bare upper chamber, roof about fifteen feet each way and a parapet.
entities.game_adaptation: Stable arena sequence or ending image inspired by the windows; stairs need not be combat traversal.

entities.title: Alien wonder
entities.name: Alien wonder
entities.description: Scarlet sand, unfamiliar colors, new organs and unearthly light make perception itself feel new.
entities.visual_facts: Opalescent highlights; immense sunlight; generous strange horizons.
entities.game_adaptation: Curiosity before commitment: keep the floor readable.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Uncanny social performance
entities.name: Uncanny social performance
entities.description: A sophisticated domestic entertainment becomes a genuine and violent supernatural event.
entities.visual_facts: Warm electric luxury followed by a repulsive grin and cold coast.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional prologue contrast, not a lengthy tutorial.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Compassion and purity
entities.name: Compassion and purity
entities.description: Joiwind’s blood exchange and Panawe’s reverence for life offer tenderness without removing the troubling later journey.
entities.visual_facts: Gentle half-tone changing skin, open gestures, white clothes.
entities.game_adaptation: Rest beats between pressure; civilians remain non-hostile.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Dominion and unstable agency
entities.name: Dominion and unstable agency
entities.description: Ifdawn’s will-users and Tydomin make freedom feel unreliable; the landscape itself shifts and interpersonal desire becomes coercion.
entities.visual_facts: Sorb eye, third arm, jagged mountains and close confrontations.
entities.game_adaptation: Fake positions and locked attacks test judgment; never steal actual control unpredictably.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Cold doctrinal certainty
entities.name: Cold doctrinal certainty
entities.description: Sant’s competing ascetics turn moral confidence into lethal obedience, followed by Maskull’s later remorse.
entities.visual_facts: Bare green snow, severe bodies, single/double forehead membranes.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional image/story beat; avoid presenting one doctrine as the game’s endorsed rule.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Haunted forest and remorse
entities.name: Haunted forest and remorse
entities.description: Wombflash’s silence and impossible scale hold Maskull’s recognition of his killings; drumming promises a stranger truth.
entities.visual_facts: Wet leaves, distant tiny sky, immense widely separated trunks and wandering mist. Red trunks/ulfire leaves come from Panawe’s earlier recollection.
entities.game_adaptation: Spare encounter rhythm with one distant recurring pulse motif.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Ecstatic, dangerous music
entities.name: Ecstatic, dangerous music
entities.description: Gleameil pursues the lake’s answer willingly; music enlarges perception but brings death and destruction.
entities.visual_facts: Ripples, moonlight, motion moving from stillness to violent water.
entities.game_adaptation: Visual pulses support play; music never becomes an unseen rhythm-game requirement.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Evolutionary excess
entities.name: Evolutionary excess
entities.description: Matterplay feels like a conversation of nature where every shape is unique and life transforms faster than it can be classified.
entities.visual_facts: Crowded varied organic profiles framed by bare stone.
entities.game_adaptation: Use bounded scenery variation with a very small actual enemy roster.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Painful passion and sacrifice
entities.name: Painful passion and sacrifice
entities.description: Lichstorm intensifies love and harm. Sullenbode’s devotion and guidance coexist with the deadly dependence of her life on Maskull’s love.
entities.visual_facts: Glow in black mist, green snow, lonely ridge and grave.
entities.game_adaptation: Garden manifestation can externalise attachment without casting Sullenbode as a monster.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Seductive false beauty
entities.name: Seductive false beauty
entities.description: Gangnet’s reassurance and Alppain’s apparent release threaten to make renunciation another pleasure inside Crystalman’s world.
entities.visual_facts: Soft blue/jale haze, charming face, pleasant landscape giving way to grin.
entities.game_adaptation: Contrast calm framing with clearly telegraphed final echoes.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Cosmic horror and unresolved struggle
entities.name: Cosmic horror and unresolved struggle
entities.description: The final windows expose spirit fragmented and trapped to feed Crystalman. Nightspore’s insight leads to renewed work and risk, not a universe restored by one blow.
entities.visual_facts: Bright shadow, green imprisoned sparks, white whirls and small tower in boundless darkness.
entities.game_adaptation: Local boss victory grants an exit and changed understanding; retain ambiguity and ongoing struggle.
entities.notes: Mood label is a research interpretation of the cited events, not a quoted statement of authorial intent.

entities.title: Magn
entities.name: Magn
entities.description: Chest tentacle through which Poolingdred people intensify love and compassion. In Ifdawn it develops into a third arm with changed emotional implications.
entities.visual_facts: Thin flexible whipcord tentacle from the heart region.
entities.game_adaptation: Character reference; no new compulsory gesture or damage upgrade.

entities.title: Breve
entities.name: Breve
entities.description: Hollow fleshy forehead organ used to read thoughts. Maskull’s changes to a sorb after entering Ifdawn.
entities.visual_facts: Plum-sized forehead protuberance with a cavity.
entities.game_adaptation: Visual transition or lore; do not make UI hide itself behind fictional telepathy.

entities.title: Poigns
entities.name: Poigns
entities.description: Paired knobs beneath the ears allow understanding and sympathy with living creatures.
entities.visual_facts: One knob on each side of the neck.
entities.game_adaptation: Anatomy sheet and compassionate silhouette.

entities.title: Sorb
entities.name: Sorb
entities.description: Will-associated forehead eye that treats the world according to personal needs and can impose transformations or domination.
entities.visual_facts: Single third eye on the brow.
entities.game_adaptation: Basis for clear projection/echo motifs; player input remains reliable.

entities.title: Ifdawn third arm
entities.name: Ifdawn third arm
entities.description: Magn develops into a muscular arm arising from the breast, strengthening security and passionate contact.
entities.visual_facts: Chest-origin third arm and hand.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional character variant, not a mandatory extra attack button.

entities.title: Sant probes and membranes
entities.name: Sant probes and membranes
entities.description: Spadevil transforms the sorb into double forehead membranes; Catice possesses a single one. Maskull’s judgment changes with these faculties.
entities.visual_facts: Flat rudimentary-eye membranes or projecting probes on the forehead.
entities.game_adaptation: Lore/portrait variants. Do not grant permanent damage progression.

entities.title: Wombflash third eye
entities.name: Wombflash third eye
entities.description: After Sant, Maskull again has a third forehead eye whose use he initially cannot identify. It is distinct from the earlier sorb in his uncertain understanding.
entities.visual_facts: Forehead eye and nerveless third arm.
entities.game_adaptation: Sensory storytelling; avoid calling every forehead eye a sorb.

entities.title: Hator’s Trifork
entities.name: Hator’s Trifork
entities.description: Hator’s three-forked symbol marks the route to Sant. Spadevil interprets stem and branches as hatred of pleasure, disentanglement, power and the cold glow of ascetic practice. Catice carries a smaller version.
entities.visual_facts: Plain forked ritual tool, austerely scaled to his body.
entities.game_adaptation: Boss candidate telegraph silhouette; not a farmable weapon tier.
entities.notes: The symbol and its doctrinal interpretation are given in chapters 11–12; Catice’s carried implement is not an independent weapon-upgrade tier.

chapter_refs.label: Chapter 11. ON DISSCOURN
chapter_refs.title: ON DISSCOURN
chapter_refs.note: Large route marker and Hator’s symbol.

entities.title: Ulfire, jale and dolm
entities.name: Ulfire, jale and dolm
entities.description: Ulfire and jale are additional primary colors described through emotional analogy; dolm combines ulfire and blue. Two sun-derived sets share blue.
entities.visual_facts: Ulfire is wild/painful by analogy; jale dreamlike/feverish/voluptuous; dolm appears in Haunte’s skin.
entities.game_adaptation: Any RGB palette is interpretive representation; never promise literally to display new primary colors.

entities.title: Changing skin and contrasting blood
entities.name: Changing skin and contrasting blood
entities.description: Tormance skin often shifts with emotion. Joiwind’s blood is milky and opalescent; Maskull’s red Earth blood is initially too heavy for the world.
entities.visual_facts: Soft opalescence contrasted with red Earth blood.
entities.game_adaptation: Character-material reference, not blood exchange as health farming.

entities.title: Crystal trees and shrubs
entities.name: Crystal trees and shrubs
entities.description: Poolingdred contains a black-trunked shrine tree with transparent leaves and crystalline plant forms with colored blossoms.
entities.visual_facts: Black branches, clear crystalline leaves and jale blossoms.
entities.game_adaptation: Scenery landmark. Crystal appearance does not itself prove allegiance to Crystalman.

entities.title: Crystal torpedo
entities.name: Crystal torpedo
entities.description: Krag’s departure machine is a crystal torpedo used to carry the three travellers through space by exploiting extraordinary rays.
entities.visual_facts: Transparent crystal craft and confined traveller arrangement.
entities.game_adaptation: Journal/cinematic prop; no vehicle level required.

entities.title: Solar back rays
entities.name: Solar back rays
entities.description: The Starkness apparatus distinguishes light’s outward rays from return rays; the last revelation relates this distinction to Muspel’s spirit and its imprisonment.
entities.visual_facts: Flasks and unusual light apparatus; final green corpuscles/white whirls are visionary.
entities.game_adaptation: Foreshadowing motif, not real astronomical science.

entities.title: Surtur’s drumming
entities.name: Surtur’s drumming
entities.description: Drumlike throbbing is first heard at the Gap of Sorgie, then calls through the forest and Ocean. Krag explains regular rhythm as the effect of passage through Crystalman’s atmosphere.
entities.visual_facts: A sound motif rather than a visible canonical drum object.
entities.game_adaptation: Audio can reinforce visible warnings; do not invent a literal drum shrine and label it canon.

chapter_refs.label: Chapter 4. THE VOICE
chapter_refs.title: THE VOICE
chapter_refs.note: Earth-frame foreshadowing: Drum Taps of Sorgie.

entities.title: Shell horn and pole raft
entities.name: Shell horn and pole raft
entities.description: Polecrab uses a shell to call his sons and a crude pole to propel the raft across the creek/sea.
entities.visual_facts: Seashell horn, rough floating platform and pole.
entities.game_adaptation: Peaceful shore kit; no new navigation controls.

entities.title: Irontick ripple instrument
entities.name: Irontick ripple instrument
entities.description: Earthrid’s instrument is the lake itself, not a violin or keyboard; its disturbed water creates the music.
entities.visual_facts: Circular reflective water, beats made with hands/feet, increasingly complex waves.
entities.game_adaptation: Represented by clearly outlined combat pulses in an alternate encounter; attack timing remains reaction-based.

entities.title: Moon-directed plant-animal
entities.name: Moon-directed plant-animal
entities.description: An upright floating living tree has a crown ring of eyelike membranes responding to moonlight. Maskull masks parts of it with leaves to steer toward Matterplay.
entities.visual_facts: Thirty feet above water, seaweedlike leaves, enormous roots and headlike crown.
entities.game_adaptation: Ecology/concept prop; transport sequence can remain a transition.

entities.title: Male stones, protecting light and skin boat
entities.name: Male stones, protecting light and skin boat
entities.description: Haunte’s boat is supported by male stones; his protecting light guards him from women. Maskull’s theft of that light precedes Haunte’s fatal kiss.
entities.visual_facts: Skin boat, two male stones, vapor/light effects and a steering pole with a luminous tip. Haunte’s forehead has a stump-like organ, not a described lamp.
entities.game_adaptation: Reference props; flight and boat-steering are not included in the ground-only campaign.

entities.title: Teargeld
entities.name: Teargeld
entities.description: Moon illuminates sea crossings and the Lichstorm ridge, making the green snow bright and directing the plant-animal.
entities.visual_facts: Bright moon, unusual colored reflections and red-black shadows.
entities.game_adaptation: Scenic night palette with readable floor contrast.

entities.title: Blodsombre
entities.name: Blodsombre
entities.description: Roughly four midday hours when Branchspell’s heat is too intense to endure, influencing shelter and travel.
entities.visual_facts: White glare, still heat, shade/shelter contrast.
entities.game_adaptation: Atmosphere and narrative compression; no real-time four-hour waiting gate.

entities.title: Matterplay life streams
entities.name: Matterplay life streams
entities.description: Streams emerging from the direction of Threal sustain prolifically changing valley life and can provoke bodily transformations.
entities.visual_facts: Clear greenish shallow bubbling water among rank unique organisms.
entities.game_adaptation: Safe boundary/scenery; no mandatory mutation roulette.

entities.title: Matterplay changing animals
entities.name: Matterplay changing animals
entities.description: Maskull watches organisms become translucent, reveal internal systems, turn invisible to sight yet palpable to emotion, and reform.
entities.visual_facts: Variable organic bodies, visible skeletal/circulatory structures and disappearing outlines.
entities.game_adaptation: Concept studies as ecology; literal invisible damaging enemies would need new fair signals and are not assumed.

entities.title: Muspel stream, green sparks and white whirls
entities.name: Muspel stream, green sparks and white whirls
entities.description: At the tower windows, a spirit stream passing through Crystalman becomes green fragments striving home and larger white whirls seeking pleasure.
entities.visual_facts: Green corpuscles imprisoned within dancing white vortices; bright shapeless shadow between world and Muspel.
entities.game_adaptation: Final projection motif; interpretation rather than measurable particles in physical space.

entities.title: Crystalman’s grin
entities.name: Crystalman’s grin
entities.description: Dead and exposed false forms repeatedly acquire the same repulsive grin, tying personal encounters to the final false creator.
entities.visual_facts: Vulgar mocking distortion imposed on formerly beautiful or solemn faces.
entities.game_adaptation: Restrained recurring reveal motif; avoid rendering every compassionate person as secretly hostile.

entities.title: Forehead jewel/light and false Surtur vision
entities.name: Forehead jewel/light and false Surtur vision
entities.description: The Lusion encounter uses a crimson jewel-like light, trumpet sound and an imposing apparition that names itself Surtur and praises the world’s rhythm.
entities.visual_facts: Red spark jewel, expanded concave cloud image and solitary trumpet note.
entities.game_adaptation: Early ambiguous vision can foreshadow deception. Do not merge this visual directly with true Krag/Surtur without caveat.

entities.title: Crimtyphon — Transmutation Tyrant
entities.name: Crimtyphon — Transmutation Tyrant
entities.description: Domination of Sature through the sorb inspires a boss that marks ground patches for delayed changes.
entities.visual_facts: Boylike controlling figure with a prominent sorb; twisted rooting victim is a separate person.
entities.game_adaptation: Small arena, one locked transformation footprint at a time, attack the exposed controller during recovery.
entities.notes: Alternate early boss; current five-level plan saves bosses for levels 4 and 5.

entities.title: Tydomin — Borrowed Will
entities.name: Tydomin — Borrowed Will
entities.description: Manipulation and attempted body exchange inspire a delayed echo and false-position encounter.
entities.visual_facts: Pale indigo-haired reptile-plate costume, sad black sorb; later twin membranes signal moral change.
entities.game_adaptation: Echo repeats a visible previous landing; actual controls never reverse or stop. The final opening breaks a local spell.
entities.notes: Alternate candidate; retain repentance instead of making her permanently evil.

entities.title: Catice — Law of Rejection
entities.name: Catice — Law of Rejection
entities.description: The single-probe ascetic and trifork suggest a severe arena with alternating refused lanes.
entities.visual_facts: Lemon-faced elder, sparse hair, deep facial ruts, single brow membrane and trifork.
entities.game_adaptation: Two predictable locked zones and a reachable recovery side; no gear check.
entities.notes: Alternate candidate or brief witness. The novel’s ideological coercion is adapted into spatial decisions.

entities.title: Earthrid and Irontick — The Fatal Music
entities.name: Earthrid and Irontick — The Fatal Music
entities.description: A musician playing a dangerous lake provides the clearest canonical instrument-based encounter concept.
entities.visual_facts: Pale musician with circular ear-like forehead organ beside circular reflective water; sparse black hair, weak face gaining crafty grandeur in moonlight.
entities.game_adaptation: Ground shoreline arena with pulses previewed visibly; never require unseen beat synchronisation.
entities.notes: Strong optional/alternate boss candidate. Current main path uses musical imagery as environment/story.

entities.title: Sullenbode’s Garden — Fabricated Attachment
entities.name: Sullenbode’s Garden — Fabricated Attachment
entities.description: Invented root-and-tether manifestation staged by Crystalman, borrowing an alluring image and the story’s dependence of life on love.
entities.visual_facts: Low external root knots, tethers and enclosing growth; a projected Sullenbode likeness stays non-damageable.
entities.game_adaptation: Attack the low external root knots only after locked tether/crescent commitments; clearing knots tears open the fabricated enclosing garden. The projected woman is never the damage target.
entities.notes: Entire garden, hostile roots and botanical boss are inventions. Sullenbode canonically guides and sacrifices; do not claim she rules this garden.

entities.title: Crystalman — The False World
entities.name: Crystalman — The False World
entities.description: A local manifested obstruction embodies the false creator’s grinning deception and imprisonment of spirit.
entities.visual_facts: Bright nebulous shadow, refracted green sparks and white whirls; any crystal humanoid is art interpretation.
entities.game_adaptation: Capture the player’s completed actual world dash and attack. Phase 1 holds one replay slot; phase 2 at most two, played sequentially from exact visible previews once. Attack a nearby slashable tether in recovery. No simultaneous solar/root attacks compete with the replay.
entities.notes: Player breaks a local manifestation and leaves; novel ending is an ongoing spiritual struggle, not Crystalman’s total destruction.

entities.title: Muremaker / Nuclamp — Suspended Will
entities.name: Muremaker / Nuclamp — Suspended Will
entities.description: Panawe’s account of a cruel sorb-user suspended by a rival suggests an arena built around an imposed holding field.
entities.visual_facts: Suspended ogrelike figure above a gulf; Nuclamp’s appearance is unspecified.
entities.game_adaptation: Ground-floor adaptation would need to remove literal fatal falling and target a visible field source.
entities.notes: Retrospective anecdote and substantial new arena logic; not selected.

entities.title: Three Figures — False Divinity
entities.name: Three Figures — False Divinity
entities.description: The colossi’s changing divine appearances suggest a false-authority set piece or projected boss.
entities.visual_facts: Three immense statues/visions, rosy light and the exposed grin.
entities.game_adaptation: Scenic revelations around a single ground combat controller; no three additional boss health bars.
entities.notes: Keep as reference imagery to avoid increasing the act’s boss count.

entities.title: Haillar Station and approach
entities.name: Haillar Station and approach
entities.description: The travellers reach Starkness on foot from Haillar Station, seven miles away; a wild lonely coastal road supplies the approach.
entities.visual_facts: The travellers reach Starkness on foot from Haillar Station, seven miles away; a wild lonely coastal road supplies the approach.
entities.game_adaptation: Railway arrival is a brief framing reference; no train-management game.

entities.title: Gap of Sorgie
entities.name: Gap of Sorgie
entities.description: A narrow sea inlet cuts the coastal cliffs. Nightspore and Maskull lie at its edge to hear the locally named Drum Taps of Sorgie from below.
entities.visual_facts: A narrow sea inlet cuts the coastal cliffs. Nightspore and Maskull lie at its edge to hear the locally named Drum Taps of Sorgie from below.
entities.game_adaptation: Optional foreshadowing tableau; sound does not replace visible combat warnings.

entities.title: North Sea coast
entities.name: North Sea coast
entities.description: Starkness stands on cliffs beside the North Sea; salt east wind, dark green white-flecked waves and plaintive gull cries contrast with Tormance.
entities.visual_facts: Starkness stands on cliffs beside the North Sea; salt east wind, dark green white-flecked waves and plaintive gull cries contrast with Tormance.
entities.game_adaptation: Earth-frame color/sound reference.

entities.title: Arcturus — fictional destination
entities.name: Arcturus — fictional destination
entities.description: The travellers name Arcturus as the destination and Tormance as the planet with its twin suns. This is the novel’s astronomical fiction.
entities.visual_facts: The travellers name Arcturus as the destination and Tormance as the planet with its twin suns. This is the novel’s astronomical fiction.
entities.game_adaptation: Sky/reference framing; not a scientific model of the real star.

entities.title: Crimtyphon’s peninsula clearing
entities.name: Crimtyphon’s peninsula clearing
entities.description: A shaded two-acre copse has a central tree, high moss couch, iron-red bubbling fountain and thorn/flower/creeper-fringed precipices. Crimtyphon transforms Sature there.
entities.visual_facts: A shaded two-acre copse has a central tree, high moss couch, iron-red bubbling fountain and thorn/flower/creeper-fringed precipices. Crimtyphon transforms Sature there.
entities.game_adaptation: Alternate transmutation-boss arena; the source’s iron-red water belongs here, not to Poolingdred’s well.
